design.site_summary: A moderately lit indoor pet-friendly living area with a curious cat requiring non-toxic greenery.
design.layout_strategy: Trailing plants on high shelves at eye level, upright structural foliage plants at mid height against the interior wall, and a low ground grazing layer within reach along the floor edge.
design.combination_logic: This combination merges soft arching fronds with broad striped foliage, contrasting dark glossy greens with silvery patterns and soft textures, providing year-round visual interest without any toxic risk.

zones.placement: on the north-facing high wall shelf, receiving 2 hours of indirect ambient daylight, safely out of direct pet reach

plants.why: Provides lush cascading green fronds suited for elevated placements.
plants.role_in_combination: Adds fine texture and a delicate trailing visual accent to the top layer.

maintenance: Water thoroughly when the top inch of soil feels dry
Mist the fronds weekly to maintain humidity
Remove any brown fronds at the base as needed

plants.why: Offers bold veined leaves and occasional bright floral bracts.
plants.role_in_combination: Serves as the main color focal point among the green foliage.

maintenance: Keep soil consistently moist but never waterlogged
Feed with half-strength liquid fertilizer monthly in spring and summer

care_instructions.frequency: every 7 to 10 days depending on ambient humidity

care_cautions: Overwatering the Calathea insignis in the mid-level zone can cause root rot and yellowing leaves.
Placing the Aphelandra squarrosa in direct intense sunlight will scorch its delicate variegated foliage.
Ensure the heavy floor planter in the grazing zone is stable so pets cannot tip it over.
design.pet_safety_note: Every plant selected in this design is completely non-toxic to cats and dogs, ensuring total safety even if your pet decides to graze on the floor-level foliage.
